access_notes.value: Self-serve for development: a PAT can be generated in the developer console on a free Asana plan, and OAuth apps are created in the developer console. A developer sandbox must be requested via a form and can take up to one week to provision (valid max one year, extensions require Legal review). Service Accounts are Enterprise-only and can only be created by Asana super admins. Script actions require Enterprise/Enterprise+. Workspace admins can block MCP client apps.
access_notes.quote: Please note that at this time, it may take up to one (1) week to process and provision your developer sandbox.

official_mcp_server.quote: The Asana MCP V2 server is available at: `https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp`.

rate_limits.value: Free domains: 150 requests/min; Paid domains: 1,500 requests/min; Search API: 60 requests/min; duplication/instantiation/export endpoints: 5 concurrent jobs per user; concurrency limiter around 50 GET or 15 write requests in flight.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Base URL is versioned (/api/1.0). A deprecations guide exists. V1 Beta MCP server (https://mcp.asana.com/sse) is deprecated and scheduled to shut down Wed 5 Aug 2026 (another official page states 05/11/2026).
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The V1 Beta MCP server `https://mcp.asana.com/sse` is deprecated and will shut down on Wed 5 Aug 2026.

verdict_reason: Asana documents a public REST API with a full OpenAPI-generated reference, and a developer can self-serve credentials by generating a PAT in the developer console, with OAuth available for multi-user apps. Rate limits are explicitly documented (150 req/min free, 1,500 req/min paid) and webhooks, a developer sandbox, and an official hosted MCP server (https://mcp.asana.com/v2/mcp) are all documented. The only friction is that a developer sandbox is requested via a form with up to a week of provisioning time, which does not gate basic API access.
open_questions: Official SDK language list was not captured: docs pages for JavaScript, Python, and client libraries were indexed but their text was not included in the evidence (only 'official client libraries' is mentioned on the rate-limits page).
Standard OAuth scope/permission list was not captured; only Service Account scopes and the MCP 'default' scope are referenced in the evidence.
REST API versioning/deprecation policy page (developers.asana.com/docs/deprecations) was indexed but not fetched; only the MCP v1 beta deprecation is evidenced here.
Official docs give conflicting MCP v1 beta sunset dates (05/11/2026 on the MCP overview page vs Wed 5 Aug 2026 on the integration guide).
No credible community/third-party MCP servers were evidenced (no GitHub repository or MCP registry results were supplied).
App Directory listing/publication review requirements for a third-party integration were not captured in the evidence.
